discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: formerly University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and quantum materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands almost perfectly flat, so that Coulomb interactions dominate kinetic energy. Jarillo-Herrero and coworkers (2018) realized this, discovering correlation-driven insulating states at integer filling and unconventional superconductivity nearby, reminiscent of doped Mott insulators. This work created an entirely new, tunable platform for strongly correlated electron physics: a single device, controlled by a gate voltage and twist angle, explores Mott-like insulators, superconductivity, strange-metal transport, orbital magnetism and, in related moire systems, fractional Chern insulators. Moire materials have transformed quantum materials research worldwide, linking band topology and strong correlations and providing decisive experimental tests for many-body theory. The combination of a precise theoretical prediction and its spectacular experimental confirmation represents a discovery of the highest importance for physics.
